page: Vultr vcg-l40s-32c-375g-96vram is a GPU-accelerated cloud server based on the x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 6448H processor featuring 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz under a shared allocation model. The system features 375.0 GB of system memory, yielding 11.72 GB per core, and includes a 2200 GB local NVMe SSD. Graphics and parallel compute acceleration are delivered by two NVIDIA L40S GPUs from the Ada Lovelace family, providing a combined total of 96 GB of VRAM.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates strong multi-core processing and memory read capabilities. It achieved a multi-core stress-ng score of 62,892.75 and a Passmark CPU score of 64,768.69. Memory read bandwidth is highly efficient, registering at 4,985.78 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 211.9 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Single-threaded compression performance is top-tier, with gzip compression reaching 35.41 GB/sec. For artificial intelligence workloads, the dual L40S GPUs deliver top-tier LLM inference speeds, processing 6,275.36 prompt tokens per second and generating 141.42 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

While the server offers high resource density and exceptional parallel processing power, certain tradeoffs exist. The CPU cores operate on a shared allocation, and single-core performance is average, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2,209.29. Additionally, large-block memory write bandwidth is average at 88.2 GB/sec. Qualitatively, this configuration represents a highly resource-dense profile, offering substantial GPU memory and system RAM relative to its CPU allocation. It is best suited for LLM inference, parallel data science pipelines, high-throughput database operations, and intensive web serving.
